summary: This program builds a playlist of songs in a list, then copies the same songs into a HashMap keyed by title and into a TreeMap, printing both so you can see that a HashMap gives no reliable ordering while a TreeMap keeps its keys sorted alphabetically.

lines.text: Map is the interface both HashMap and TreeMap implement, so the same variable type can hold either one.
TreeMap is the sorted map implementation; importing it alongside HashMap is what lets the program compare the two behaviours side by side.
The list is declared as the List interface but created as an ArrayList, a habit that keeps the rest of the code independent of the chosen implementation.
Each Song object bundles title, artist, genre, and an energy level from 1 to 10 into one value the list can store.
The enhanced for loop walks the list in insertion order, which is exactly the order the songs were added.
A map stores key-value pairs; here each song's title is the key used to look up the whole Song object.
put stores one pair, so this loop transfers every song from the list into the map under its own title.
keySet returns all the keys in the map, and a HashMap hands them back in an order determined by hash codes rather than by anything meaningful to a reader.
get looks up the value for a key, and the Song is printed through its toString method as part of the concatenated string.
Passing an existing map to the TreeMap constructor copies all its pairs in, and the TreeMap immediately arranges them by the natural ordering of the String keys.
The same loop over the same data now prints titles in alphabetical order, which is the whole point of the comparison.
